title: Session lifecycle undefended: 24h stateless HS256 JWT survives logout, password change, MFA disable/unbind and account lockout because AuthMiddleware never loads the user row (severity downgraded from high: exploitation requires a token already stolen via a separately-reported weakness, so this is a defense-in-depth / incident-response gap, not an independent account-takeover primitive)
evidence: backend/internal/admin/auth.go:152-155 `func (s *Server) logout(c *gin.Context) { s.recordOp(c, "login", "auth", "logout", nil, nil); s.ok(c, nil) }` - logout writes an audit row only. auth.go:181 `s.db.Model(&model.AdminUser{}).Where("id = ?", u.ID).Update("password_hash", string(hash))` - password change invalidates nothing. auth.go:278-279 `s.db.Model(&model.AdminUser{}).Where("id = ?", uid).Updates(map[string]any{ "mfa_secret": "", "mfa_enabled": false, ...})` and users.go:48-49 (admin-side unbind) clear the MFA secret without touching sessions. backend/internal/auth/jwt.go:21 `ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now().Add(24 * time.Hour)),` and the Claims struct at jwt.go:11-15 carries only UserID/Username/RegisteredClaims (RegisteredClaims.ID/jti is never populated by Issue, jwt.go:17-27). backend/internal/admin/middleware.go:23-30 `claims, err := auth.Parse(s.secret, token)` ... `c.Set("operator", claims.Username); c.Set("userID", claims.UserID)` - zero DB access, so the user row is never re-validated. Verified absent: grep over backend/ for `jti|revok|blacklist|denylist|token_version|session_version` -> no matches (only an unrelated comment at backend/internal/db/db.go:55 for `session`); model.AdminUser (backend/internal/model/model.go:13-26) has no token_version/role/enabled column and model.AllModels() (model.go:296-303) registers no session/denylist table; auth.Issue has exactly one call site (auth.go:125) and auth.Parse exactly two (middleware.go:23 and admin/auditws.go:31 `claims, err := auth.Parse(s.secret, c.Query("token"))` on the route registered without AuthMiddleware at routes.go:118 `api.GET("/audit/ws", s.auditWS)`).
impact: The session lifecycle has no server-side control point. Logout is a no-op that the UI renders as 'logged out' (frontend/src/layouts/MainLayout.tsx:184-192 clears localStorage after POST /auth/logout returns code 0), changing the password or unbinding MFA does not disturb an outstanding bearer token, and the project's own lockout (auth.go:113-122 sets locked_until; model.go:28-30 IsLocked) is consulted only at login (auth.go:38), so a locked account's already-issued token keeps returning 200 across all ~85 AuthMiddleware routes (routes.go:43-148). The only containment left is out-of-band: rotate JWT_SECRET and restart every instance, because Server.secret is fixed at construction (admin/server.go:30,38) and POST /config/reload does not touch it (admin/configstatus.go:42-50). Impact is bounded and secondary: the JWT is already a full-admin credential (AdminUser has no roles), so this finding prolongs an intrusion that some other flaw opened rather than opening it, and expiry caps the window at 24h from issuance.
exploit_sketch: Precondition (not supplied by this finding): the attacker holds a valid admin JWT - via the separately-filed default/committed JWT_SECRET (authn-1), a fronting proxy that logs full URIs for `GET /api/admin/v1/audit/ws?token=<JWT>` as emitted by frontend/src/hooks/useAuditStream.ts:65 (frontend-2), or localStorage['llm-router-guard.auth.v1'] (auth.ts:9) under a future XSS (frontend-1). Then: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" :8080/api/admin/v1/providers` succeeds; the defender POSTs /auth/logout (auth.go:152-155 -> audit row only), PUTs /auth/password (auth.go:181 -> password_hash only), POSTs /account/mfa/disable (auth.go:278-279) and/or lets 5 bad passwords trip the lockout (auth.go:117-120); every one of those returns {"code":0} and each is recorded in the operation audit, yet middleware.go:15-32 still authenticates the stolen token because it only calls auth.Parse and never loads the user row. The attacker keeps full admin (including POST /backups/restore, PUT /settings/security, DELETE /apikeys/:id) until exp (+24h) or until an operator rotates JWT_SECRET and restarts the process, which also logs out every legitimate admin.
mitigations_checked: Expiry is enforced by golang-jwt v5.2.1 default validators, so exposure is bounded at 24h and there is no refresh-token long-tail. alg confusion is blocked (jwt.go:31 `if _, ok := t.Method.(*jwt.SigningMethodHMAC); !ok`). The JWT is not stored in a cookie and there is no CORS middleware, so a cross-origin page cannot silently attach it. This product never logs the query string: cmd/server/main.go:89 uses `engine := gin.New()` (no gin.Logger) and the bespoke access log at main.go:109,116-117 prints `path := c.Request.URL.Path`, not RawURI/RawQuery, so the /audit/ws token exposure is external-proxy-only. There is a global kill switch the original finding omitted: rotating JWT_SECRET and restarting invalidates every outstanding token. Attacker activity remains attributable and visible: server.go:94-97 `audit.LogOp(s.db, operatorOf(c), ... clientIP(c) ...)` on every mutation, readable at GET /audit/operations (routes.go:114), so the 'looks successful in the UI' framing overstates defender blindness. No XSS sink found (grep over frontend/src for dangerouslySetInnerHTML|innerHTML|eval\(|new Function -> zero matches), so the XSS theft premise is hypothetical. No rate limiting or IP binding on admin API bearer use; no re-auth gate on sensitive endpoints (PUT /settings, /backups/restore, /apikeys) - confirmed absent.
corrections_to_original_finding: Three claims do not hold and were removed from the impact statement: (1) 'unlock the account' is not an incident-response containment action - users.go:54-64 clears failed_logins/locked_until, i.e. it grants login, so it never should have been in the list of actions that 'should stop an intrusion'; (2) 'even deleting ... the account leaves the bearer authorized' describes a capability that does not exist - there is no create/delete/disable-user endpoint (routes.go:133-135 exposes only GET /users, POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa, POST /users/:id/unlock; users.go is 65 lines; admins are bootstrapped once at cmd/server/main.go:164-184 and bootstrapAdmin returns early if any user exists), so account deletion is out-of-band SQLite surgery, not a defeated in-product control; the 'locking' half is accurate. (3) 'no mechanism to add revocation later without a schema change' is too strong - a denylist keyed on (uid, iat) needs a new table but no change to AdminUser, and IssuedAt is already populated at jwt.go:22 while RegisteredClaims.ID (jti) already exists and merely goes unset. Also note double-counting: the WS query-string JWT used here to justify 'high' is the identical vector scored medium in frontend-2, and the forgeable-default-secret and missing-CSP theft routes are scored separately in authn-1 and frontend-1.
severity_rationale: Rubric: high = authed-but-severe or account takeover; medium = defense-in-depth gap with real impact. This finding confers no privilege the stolen token does not already confer, and no code path in this finding lets an attacker who lacks the token obtain it; it only removes the defender's ability to shorten an exposure opened by another vulnerability. That is the textbook definition of a session-management defense-in-depth gap, and the real impact (logout is fake, credential changes do not revoke, lockout does not reach live sessions, only a global secret rotation + restart works) keeps it above low. Downgraded high -> medium; the remediation recommendation is retained as filed.
recommendation: Add `token_version uint` to admin_users, embed it in Claims, bump it on logout/changePassword/mfaDisable/unbindUserMfa/delete-user (and add the missing disable/delete-user control), and compare it in AuthMiddleware after loading the user row - that single load also fixes the lockout-does-not-reach-sessions gap. Alternatively shorten access tokens to 5-15 min with a server-side refresh record in the existing mfaStore (redis_mfa.go already supports cluster-wide tickets). Replace the long-lived JWT in the /audit/ws query string (auditws.go:31, useAuditStream.ts:65) with a short-lived one-time WS ticket or a Sec-WebSocket-Protocol value. Also make the 24h TTL configurable - it is currently hard-coded at jwt.go:21.
